clue.text: A party in the money, evergreen

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for money

parts.note: cash is money
Lab is short for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A political party flush with funds stays forever green.
explanation.definitionFit: The calabash tree of tropical America is an evergreen bearing gourd fruits.

clue.text: See 24
See 11
Gifted individual scoring mark

definitions.meaning: someone with innate talent is called a born one of these
in a musical score, the sign cancelling a sharp or flat

explanation.definitionFit: Natural means a born talent, and also the musical sign restoring a note to unaltered pitch.

clue.text: Price, of course, offers little time to animated character in distress

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: in puts the cartoon figure inside the word for distress

parts.note: woe is distress
a toon is a cartoon character

explanation.surface: Someone offers a cartoon figure a moment while it is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price, of course' means odds offered at the racecourse, not a path of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting odds are a price quoted at the racecourse, and these odds are a common example.

clue.text: Part of a tree's flower starts to evolve, developing within mountain

indicators.note: within places the river and initials inside the word for a heap

parts.note: a pile, as in a mountain of washing, is a great heap
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Nene is an English river

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A bloom slowly evolves while growing on a mountainside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, the Nene in eastern England; 'starts to' gives E and D from 'evolve, developing'. The definition 'Part of a tree's' stands for the noun with its possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer's leaf is a slender needle, one part of the tree.

clue.text: Greek for "hand" originally contrived to encapsulate glove puppet

indicators.note: to encapsulate means the jumbled letters wrap around the handwear
contrived signals the letters are rearranged into a made-up order
originally takes the first letter of the quoted word

parts.note: a mitt is a glove

explanation.surface: A Greek word for hand is invented to describe a glove puppet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for the Greek word for hand, but nothing is translated: only the first letter of the quoted word is used, and 'glove puppet' splits, the glove going into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muppets' green frog is the most famous hand puppet of all.

clue.text: A fool among the masses reaching a Canadian province

indicators.note: among puts the fool inside the crowd

parts.note: the mob is the masses
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool joins a crowd heading for a part of Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The prairie province lies in central Canada between Ontario and Saskatchewan.

clue.text: Get your rotten tomatoes now …

parts.note: read as a shop cry urging buyers before supplies run out, but also as a call to pelt someone pilloried in the old wooden restraints

explanation.surface: A trader shouts that bruised tomatoes are on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The stocks were wooden frames where offenders were pelted with rotten fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales slogan urging customers to buy before the goods are gone.

clue.text: See 24
Medico must start removing last of privates in operation — on the other hand, no need to worry!

indicators.note: in operation suggests surgery but signals the letters being worked into a new order
removing takes the named letter out of the three words before shuffling
last of takes the final letter of privates

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, as on the other hand does

explanation.surface: A doctor must begin surgery on someone's private parts, but says there is nothing to fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' drops one S from MEDICO MUST START; 'in operation' shuffles the rest to TRUSTMEIMADOCT.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase is a reassurance offered as though by a professional, telling the listener not to fret.

clue.text: Look for bird

definitions.meaning: a quick glance, as in 'have a look'

explanation.definitionFit: A gander is British slang for a look, and also a male goose.

clue.text: Wrong story written up about firm garment

parts.note: duff means faulty or wrong

indicators.note: about has the turned word go round the firm
written up in a down entry means the word reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: a tale is a story
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A false tale is written up about some company's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns TALE into ELAT, which goes 'about' CO.
explanation.definitionFit: This hooded toggle coat is a heavy woollen garment.

clue.text: A further exaggerated, backward, chubby, naked boy

parts.note: more means further or additional

indicators.note: backward means the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, exaggerated

explanation.surface: A plump little boy is described with backward exaggeration.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a cherub or cupid, painted as a plump naked infant.

clue.text: See 7
Rival work, work of model

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
what a model does is posing

explanation.surface: Two rival kinds of work compete, one a model's.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, opposing describes a rival side or team.

clue.text: See 22 down
Left out of order

definitions.meaning: left is the side that is not the other one
out of order means unacceptable or wrong

explanation.definitionFit: Left is literally the other side from right; out of order means wrong.

clue.text: About to go in wash, underwater one can't do it

indicators.note: to go in puts the short preposition inside the washing word

parts.note: to bathe is to wash
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: About to take a bath, someone notes what is impossible underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing air into the lungs is impossible underwater.

clue.text: Birdie is sick as a parrot?

definitions.meaning: in golf, a hole played in one shot fewer than standard
the British idiom for feeling disappointed, here taken literally as feeling unwell

explanation.definitionFit: A golf birdie is one stroke below the standard score; feeling below standard means unwell.

clue.text: Mark classical art only?

definitions.meaning: to mark is to write down in symbols
the Tate galleries are famed for modern art

explanation.walkthrough: Read the second part as NO TATE: the Tate is London's best-known gallery of modern art.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to set down in written symbols, as one marks music on a stave.

clue.text: 24 across-ly 24 across

definitions.meaning: the adverb made from the answer to 24 across, meaning rather or quite
the answer to 24 across in the sense good-looking

explanation.definitionFit: Pretty means fairly, as in pretty good, and also good-looking, a sense of the other answer.

clue.text: Rubbish seen round temporary dwelling — the conclusion? Don't copy it

indicators.note: round means the rubbish wraps the shelter

parts.note: pap is worthless nonsense
a tent is a temporary dwelling
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Rubbish strewn around a campsite tent at the close of the festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a warning stamped on a new invention: copying it may infringe.
explanation.definitionFit: The label warns others that a protection claim on the invention is in progress, so do not imitate it.

clue.text: See 9
Shooting ducks, perhaps a reasonable target?

definitions.meaning: a fairground stall where one shoots at moving toy ducks
someone or something legitimately open to attack or ridicule

explanation.definitionFit: A fairground shooting gallery is a sideshow, and a legitimate target is the familiar idiom.

clue.text: Parting of lips identifies the 16 view

indicators.note: parting suggests the words are split open to reveal a run of letters inside

explanation.surface: Lips parting reveal what someone thinks.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' is OPPOSING, so the definition reads 'the opposing view'.
explanation.definitionFit: The other side of an argument is its reverse face, like the B side of a record.

clue.text: Exercise right to entertain?

annotationWithheld.why: Exercise right to entertain? (5): 'entertain' must be split as 'enter' (container indicator) plus TAIN (fodder), one word doing two jobs, which the grammar cannot express

clue.text: Where no men measure up, bearing twins internally

indicators.note: bearing internally means the measure carries the pair inside it
bearing internally means the measure carries the pair inside it

parts.note: height is the measure upward
twins read as a matching pair of letters, two Ns

explanation.surface: Somewhere men fail to measure up, women carrying twins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twins' gives two identical letters, here NN.
explanation.definitionFit: A party for the bride and her female friends before a wedding excludes men.
